blocks.text: How Matthew 25 fits with Matthew 24 is debated. One reading understands Matthew 24–25 as a connected sequence bringing together temple destruction, tribulation, the coming of the Son of Man, unknown timing, readiness, stewardship, and judgment. From that perspective, the scenes in this chapter are not isolated sayings: preparedness for an awaited return and accountability for what has been entrusted recur across them. The servants-and-money story also draws on an estate setting of servants, a traveling master, financial dealings, and accounting that resonates with an unequal agrarian Roman-Palestinian economy.
